To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

TACT provides a toolkit for tunably adjusting availability/consistency levels of replicated Internet services, enabling differentiated availability, and quality of service, and further enabling Internet services to dynamically choose availability/consistency and trade consistency for performance.
TACT provides Internet services with a flexible and dynamic approach to choose their availability/consistency levels, and that TACT makes it feasible to dynamically trade consistency and performance.

1) TACT is a toolkit that enables Internet services to choose their own availability and consistency, 2) TACT makes it easier to build highly-available and fault tolerant Internet services, 3) TACT makes Internet services more robust to network partitions, and 4) TACT makes the Internet more robust.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of a toolkit for building replicated Internet services with tunable availability and/or consistency.

the design of the next generation of replicated Internet services, where availability/consistency are dynamically tunable and differentiated, and where performance is improved at the expense of consistency.
the fundamental issue of building replicated Internet services with tunable availability/consistency properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TACT is a toolkit for tunability of availability and consistency in replicated Internet services.
TACT enables Internet services to flexibily trade availability/consistency for performance.
we have presented a toolkit for building Internet services that dynamically choose their availability/consistency and performance tradeoffs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

TACT provides Internet services with the ability to choose their own availability and consistency tradeoff levels and to dynamically change them, and thus, to achieve the best availability/consistency performance.
TACT provides a toolkit to build replicated Internet services that can dynamically trade availability and consistency.
TACT enables Internet services to achieve the best availability/consistency performance tradeoffs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Internet services can be built in a more flexible, dynamic, and adaptive manner, and that this flexibility can lead to significant performance improvements.
Internet services can be built using TACT, and the availability/consistency of the services can be dynamically and adaptively tuned according to the application needs.

the design of Internet services must be aware of the availability/consistency issue and must be able to dynamically tune the availability/consistence tradeoffs to meet the requirements of the application.
